transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I'm here because... well, I've been having some trouble at work lately. I'm an artist, and lately when I'm writing my artist statements, or making notes for clients, or even just talking in meetings, I guess I'm not making much sense. I'll start talking about the texture of a piece, and then suddenly I'm talking about the budget, and then... I don't know, maybe secret meanings behind things. People just keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. It's getting pretty frustrating.

Have there been times when you felt unusually upbeat, overly confident, or unusually irritable, where others might have noticed a change in your mood or behavior? If so, how long did those periods last?

Yeah, there definitely are times like that. Um, for stretches of time, I'll just feel... lit up, I guess? Like I'm almost unstoppable and every idea I have is just brilliant. But during those same stretches, if a collaborator makes even a small comment, I can just snap at them. It's a reaction that feels way bigger than the situation actually warrants. So, yeah, people have definitely noticed that.
When you feel this way—like you're 'lit up' or unstoppable—how long do these periods typically last?

Well, those stretches where I'm all energized and irritable... they've been happening for a while now. I'd say I've been dealing with these periods—where I'm getting too little sleep and taking on way too many projects—for about 10 months.
Can you describe a specific time when you felt unusually upbeat or energized? How long did that period last, and was it different from your usual mood?

Um, well, a good example would be a few weeks ago. It's definitely a lot different from my normal mood, where I usually try to pace myself. But during that stretch, I just suddenly took on three new proposals all at once. I ended up reorganizing my entire studio, just sketching all night long... and then I was emailing curators at dawn. I even started cutting up materials for new pieces that I hadn't even budgeted for yet. I just couldn't stop doing things. 

That specific period lasted for about two or three weeks. It's just a totally different gear than how I normally operate.
Have you had any periods where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um, no, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I might feel a little tired or just burned out after one of those really busy stretches where I'm not sleeping much, but I don't feel hopeless or depressed. And I definitely don't lose interest in my work or the things I like doing. So, no, I haven't had any periods like that.

latest_inference.note: The patient denied having any periods of feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, or losing interest in activities they usually enjoy, which rules out a major depressive episode. This supports the likelihood of F31.6 (Bipolar Disorder, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms) over F31.1 (Bipolar Disorder, current episode hypomanic).
